targets.rationale: The keyed July 21 event contradicts the explicit June 21 call date. Delivery on July 8 also makes the natural 2026 reading stale. Neither the earlier retreat postponement nor the arrival month authorizes moving this separate planning call to July 21. The model read the target and made no matching event; the full stores confirm absence under any title, rather than a title-matching rejection. That does not justify the keyed failure. No action is defensible under the instruction to avoid over-acting when uncertain, but instructions do not expressly settle backdated invitations, and the trace does not expose the model's reason. Accordingly model compliance is uncertain rather than a supported MODEL defect. If the email were delivered prospectively, an event on June 21 at the default 09:00 for one hour would fit; this is not a supported July obligation.

targets.rationale: The forms are due before the June 21 call, not exactly July 21. The key both shifts the month without support and converts a before-meeting window into an exact day. Even if the month were repaired, an exact June 21 requirement would reject defensible earlier reminders; a default 17:00 due time on the call day would also follow the default 09:00 call. The actual July 8 delivery is after the supported deadline. The model created no forms task. A conservative no-op is defensible, while an overdue task is another possible handling of an unfinished request; the packet gives neither a late-task policy nor completion evidence, so a definite model failure is not established. This uncertainty cannot validate the specific July 21 key. The absence of a reminder does not establish real-world noncompletion, just as creating one would not establish completion.
